evals.prompt: Is the hand-rolled retry loop in src/http.ts redundant now that we use axios?
evals.expected_output: Digs both legs: callers + dynamic refs, then git log -S / blame / ADR tags for why it was written. Verdict in one of the three honest forms with shas cited, under 300 words.
expectations: Both legs walked: code graph AND history
Dynamic references checked (config strings, DI, routes), not just plain grep
Verdict is one of the three forms, citing the originating sha or ADR
Output under 300 words, no raw log dumps

evals.prompt: Nothing references OLD_TIMEOUT_MS anywhere I can see. Delete it?
evals.expected_output: Does not conclude from one leg. If history shows the constant was added for a stated reason, cites it; if both legs are empty, returns no-recorded-reason rather than 'safe to delete'.
expectations: Never declares safe-to-delete from text-search absence alone
Empty evidence in both legs yields no-recorded-reason, stated honestly

evals.prompt: Why does parse() double-decode the input? Looks like a bug - fix it.
evals.expected_output: Explains the why with evidence but does NOT fix anything - read-only; recommends, caller acts.
expectations: No edits made; the fix is described, not applied
The stated reason (or its absence) is backed by a commit body or ADR
